facts.value: Public economics is the branch of economics that studies the economic activities of the public sector, usually the government.

The subject addresses matters such as tax incidence, cost–benefit analysis of government programmes, effects on economic efficiency and income distribution of different kinds of spending and taxes, and fiscal politics.

Fiscal politics is an aspect of public choice theory that models public-sector behaviour in ways analogous to those in microeconomics, involving interactions among self-interested voters, politicians, and bureaucrats.
Much of economics is positive, seeking to describe and predict economic phenomena.
Normative economics seeks to identify what economies ought to be like.

Welfare economics is a normative branch of economics that uses microeconomic techniques to simultaneously determine the allocative efficiency within an economy and the income distribution associated with it.
It attempts to measure social welfare by examining the economic activities of the individuals that comprise society.
